chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad Al-Basri, from 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman Al-Asam, from Hammad (known as) Dhil Nab, from Rumi, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What do you say about one who visits your father while in fear?' He replied: 'Allah will grant him safety on the Day of Great Terror, and the angels will receive him with glad tidings, and it will be said to him: Do not fear nor grieve. This is your day in which you achieve success.'

key_terms.الْفَزَعِ الْأَكْبَرِ: The Great Terror (a specific term for the Day of Judgment in Shia eschatology)
key_terms.زَارَ: To visit (specifically referring to Ziyarah, the ritual visitation of shrines)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam Husayn's shrine while in fear?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this narration from Zurarah to highlight the spiritual merit of performing Ziyarah despite external anxieties, linking the physical act of visiting Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) with eschatological security. The promise of being greeted by angels with 'Do not fear nor grieve' directly echoes the Quranic assurance for the righteous, emphasizing that the courage to visit the shrine in times of turmoil serves as a precursor to divine relief on the Day of Resurrection.
